definitions.explanation: A prefix attached to nouns to indicate only one of a pair or set, or that something is incomplete or one-sided. Often implies an imbalance or that the counterpart is absent.

examples.japanese: {片手|かたて}で{荷物|にもつ}を{持|も}つ。
examples.english: Hold the luggage with one hand.

examples.japanese: {片足|かたあし}で{立|た}つのは{意外|いがい}と{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Standing on one foot is surprisingly difficult.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}は{片方|かたほう}の{意見|いけん}しか{反映|はんえい}していないので、もう{一方|いっぽう}の{側|がわ}にも{聞|き}いてみよう。
examples.english: His account only reflects one side's opinion, so let's hear from the other side too.

notes:
A productive prefix meaning "one of a pair" or "one-sided." Attaches directly to nouns, especially body parts and paired objects, to indicate only one is involved.

COMPOUNDS:
- {片手|かたて}: one hand
- {片足|かたあし}: one foot/leg
- {片目|かため}: one eye
- {片耳|かたみみ}: one ear
- {片方|かたほう}: one side; one of a pair
- {片道|かたみち}: one way (trip)
- {片思|かたおも}い: unrequited love
- {片付|かたづ}ける: to tidy up; to put away
- {片隅|かたすみ}: a corner; an out-of-the-way spot

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {半|はん}: half — indicates an equal division into two (e.g., {半分|はんぶん}), while {片|かた} implies one of a natural pair
- {一方|いっぽう}: one side — a standalone noun/adverb rather than a prefix; used more abstractly

USAGE:
When {片|かた} modifies a relationship or action, it often carries a sense of incompleteness or imbalance. {片思|かたおも}い (one-sided love) implies the feeling is not returned. {片付|かたづ}ける originally meant to put things to one side, hence "tidy up."
